articles.title: Apple Prepares to Debut First AI Features in China in December
articles.description: Apple Inc. is gearing up to release its artificial intelligence platform in mainland China, following a lengthy regulatory delay that has kept the company’s AI features out of one of its most important markets.

articles.title: The AI race is back on
articles.description: Last week, Anthropic and OpenAI looked like they had the AI race to themselves, pulling ahead with increasingly powerful models that left their rivals in the dust. Google seemed hopelessly far behind, while Meta, despite spending billions to revive its floundering AI ambitions, had yet to establish itself as a serious contender. Even the latest models coming out of China, impressive as they were, appeared to be playing catch-up. Then, in the space of a few days, everything changed. articles.summary: Last week, Anthropic and OpenAI looked like they had the AI race to themselves, pulling ahead with increasingly powerful models that left their rivals in the dust. Google seemed hopelessly far behind, while Meta, despite spending billions to revive its floundering AI ambitions, had yet to establish itself as a serious contender. Even the latest models coming out of China, impressive as they were, appeared to be playing catch-up. Then, in the space of a few days, everything changed. Google and Meta both unveiled frontier models they claim can go toe to toe with the best from OpenAI and Anthropic.

articles.title: How Qualcomm’s Legal Win Over Arm Could Reshape the Long-Term Thesis for QCOM Investors
articles.description: Earlier this month, a federal jury in Delaware found that Arm Holdings breached a key architectural licensing agreement with Qualcomm and interfered with its business relationship with Meta Platforms, awarding Qualcomm nominal damages of US$2 but confirming its right to continue custom CPU development under the license. The verdict primarily strengthened Qualcomm’s legal footing and business flexibility as Arm shifts its business model, clarifying Qualcomm’s ability to pursue its Oryon CPU...

articles.title: AI chiefs sound alarm on security risks
articles.description: Google DeepMind co-founder Demis Hassabis cautioned that recent AI-driven cyberattacks were “early warning shots”, as more serious incidents could emerge over time unless companies and governments stepped up efforts to secure AI systems.
